name: Find a student or staff member from the header, from anywhere in the system
priorityReason: The front desk needs to reach a record while a parent is standing at the counter.

goal.actor: Super Admin, School Admin, Principal, Accounts, Staff or Coordinator
goal.capability: to find any student or staff member by name or number from any screen
goal.outcome: I reach the record without knowing which list it lives in

secondaryActors.involvement: Use the same search within their own row scope.
Searches across branches for school-wide oversight.
Searches across all branches when supporting the school.

additional.description: A keyboard shortcut focuses the search box from any screen.

preconditions.condition: The actor's role permits reaching student or staff records at all.
Student or staff records exist within the actor's branch scope.

postConditions: The actor is on the profile of the record they were looking for, or has been told plainly that nothing matched.
No record outside the actor's role and branch scope was returned, displayed or made discoverable by the search.
The search term and the record opened are recorded in the audit log, so patterns of looking up personal data can be reviewed afterwards.
No student or staff record is created, changed or deactivated. Searching is a read.

screens.name: Search results panel
screens.defaultSort: Best match first, students before staff on an equal match
visibleTo: The same roles as the search box

dataFields.name: Search text
dataFields.validation: Minimum 3 characters. Trimmed, case- and accent-insensitive. Matches name, roll number, student ID and staff ID (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Record type
dataFields.validation: Narrows the search. Defaults to both.

dataFields.name: Include inactive
dataFields.validation: Includes left, struck-off and former staff records, each marked as such (BR-5).

entities.notes: Name, roll number, student ID, class, section, status.
Records the search term and the record opened, since this reaches personal data across the whole school.

permissions.rowScope: Own branch, or another when switched per branch-scope.
Students in classes within their remit only.

permissions.notes: A Teacher reaches their students through their own class lists, which is a narrower and safer path.

businessRules.rule: Results are limited to the records the actor's role and branch already permit. Global search widens reach across modules, never across permissions.
A result is never returned that the actor could not open by navigating to it, so the search cannot be used to discover the existence of a record.
Matching covers name, roll number, student ID and staff ID. These are the system-issued identifiers a person can be asked to quote.
Each result shows its record type, so a student and a staff member with the same name are not confused.
Inactive records are excluded unless the actor asks for them, and are clearly marked when shown, so a struck-off student is never mistaken for an enrolled one.
A maximum of twenty results is shown, with the total count and a link to the full list for a narrower search.
Selecting a result opens that record's profile, not a filtered list.
Search runs after three characters and is debounced, so a query is not issued on every keystroke.
The search term and the record opened are written to the audit log, because this feature reaches personal data across the whole school.
Where the actor's scope spans several branches, each result carries its branch name, since two branches may hold pupils of the same name.

basicFlow.actor: Staff / Accounts / School Admin / Coordinator / Principal / Super Admin
basicFlow.navigation: Any authenticated screen → Header → Global search box
basicFlow.userAction: Types a name or number into the search box.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Opens the results panel over the current screen.
Waits for typing to settle, then searches student and staff records within the actor's role and branch scope.
Lists up to twenty matches with record type, class or department, status and, where the scope spans branches, the branch name.

basicFlow.actor: Staff / Accounts / School Admin / Coordinator / Principal / Super Admin
basicFlow.navigation: Search results panel → Student profile or Staff profile

basicFlow.systemResponse: Writes the audit entry naming the term searched and the record opened.

alternateFlows.behaviour: Twenty are shown with the total count and a link to the full student or staff list carrying the same term (BR-6).
The single result is still listed rather than opened automatically, so the actor confirms they have the right person before a record is opened.

alternateFlows.condition: The actor's scope spans several branches
alternateFlows.behaviour: Each result carries its branch name alongside the record type (BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: The actor asks for inactive records
alternateFlows.behaviour: Left, struck-off and former staff records are included and each is marked as such (BR-5).

exceptions.systemResponse: No search runs and the results panel does not open.
The panel shows its empty state naming the term searched, per screen-states.
exceptions.messageShown: No student or staff member matches that.

exceptions.condition: The search takes longer than 10 seconds
exceptions.systemResponse: The request is abandoned and any previous results stay on screen.
exceptions.messageShown: Search is taking longer than usual. Try a fuller name or a roll number.

exceptions.condition: The record was deactivated between the search and the selection
exceptions.messageShown: That record is no longer available.

exceptions.condition: The role may not use global search
exceptions.systemResponse: The search box is not rendered in the header at all.

exceptions.condition: The actor selects a result outside their row scope
exceptions.systemResponse: The request is refused server-side, per role-based-access.
exceptions.messageShown: You do not have permission to view this record.

sideEffects.effect: Search terms and opened records are visible in the audit trail, so unusual patterns of looking up personal data can be reviewed.

useCases.name: Login
useCases.why: Supplies the role and branch scope every result is filtered by.

useCases.name: Role-based access control
useCases.why: Decides who may search and which records are in scope.

useCases.name: Audit trail and activity log
useCases.why: Receives the search and open entries.

outOfScope.item: Searching within a single list, which each list handles itself
Searching fee, library, inventory or attendance records

departures.requirement: Results return within 1 second across 10,000 student and 500 staff records.
Global search audit entries are retained 12 months, matching the default retention.

openQuestions.question: Should Teachers be given global search limited to their own students?
openQuestions.assumption: No — they reach their students through class lists.

openQuestions.question: Should the guardian's contact number be matchable, given it is a contact rather than an identifier?
openQuestions.assumption: No. Only system-issued identifiers and names are matched (BR-3).

openQuestions.question: Is twenty the right result cap?
openQuestions.assumption: Yes, with the total count shown alongside.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
